en: The Thousand-Turn Dharani, the Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìtōng of Zǒngchí Monastery during the Great Táng Dynasty. *Namo* A-ra-ta-na da-la-ye ya (yá) na-mo. 1.

*Namo* A-ra-ta-na da-la-ye ya (yá) na-mo. (Note: The provided text contains a partial transliteration of the opening homage: *Namo A-ra-ta-na da-la-ye ya na-mo*, corresponding to *Namo Ratnatrayāya namo*. The "thousand turns" refers to the specific recitation practice of this dharani.)

The turning seal is identical to the heart seal of Avalokiteśvara, except that the toes differ from the fingers: extend the four toes and cross them backward,
pressing them inward against one another.
Bend the left thumb and insert it into the middle of the index finger;
extend the right thumb straight,
pointing inward without bending it.
Join the two arms together;
form the two legs in the shape of a cross,
with the right leg standing upright and the left knee bent outward.
The crossbow is positioned across the body, bent toward the left side.
Place the heart-seal (mudrā) before the right breast, but do not let it touch the breast.

Maintain a smiling countenance with the head turned toward the right hand seal; this is identical to the heart-seal of Avalokiteśvara, with the exception that the method for the body and feet differs. On the fifteenth day of every month, bathe in a clean room.
Form the hand-seal (*mudrā*) and recite the mantra;
this shall extinguish the four grave offenses and the five heinous crimes. This seal was translated by Master Atikūṭa.
It is called "The Thousand Turns."
Having recited this mantra, evil karma is extinguished;
upon reaching seven recitations, the five heinous crimes are extinguished;
if ten full recitations are completed, there is no sin that is not extinguished.
Regarding the method for beholding Avalokiteśvara adorned with various ornaments after one hundred thousand recitations:
during the seven days when first performing the rite,
one may consume only milk gruel, ghee, curd, white cakes, and non-glutinous rice.
One must not consume salt, sauce, or vegetables;
on the final day, one must not eat at all.
On the night of the fifteenth, one should remain with an empty stomach.
Before the Buddha, he recited mantras incessantly without a fixed number;
seeing the image move and sway, it uttered a voice, crying out, "Excellent! (Sādhu).
A brilliant light will be emitted.
Furthermore, by placing genuine jewels and precious objects upon the head of the mantra-practitioner,
one will immediately know that the rite has been successfully accomplished.
Having beheld Avalokiteśvara face-to-face,
one shall fulfill all virtuous aspirations.
Furthermore, those who see Avalokiteśvara adorned with various ornaments in a dream during sleep [shall likewise attain these benefits].
All virtuous deeds shall be accomplished,
and all evil karma shall be extinguished.
Even those who merely recite it directly shall attain the eradication of their transgressions.
When one wishes to travel to the east or west,
one should first recite the mantra over one’s hands seven times and rub them upon the face.
Wherever one goes, no calamities or misfortunes shall occur, provided that one remains pure and constantly recites it according to the Dharma without fail.
One shall attain the first bhūmi.
If there is a woman who can recite and uphold this,
she will later become a man and never again receive such a female form.
First, having prepared the altar and completed the arrangements for the offerings,
one should then recite the mantra. The altar shall measure sixteen cubits on each of its four sides and be constructed with four tiers.
The characteristics of the enclosures are such that they are white on the outside and four colors on the inside;
each has a single layer in the manner of a wall,
which constitutes the eight layers.
The five directions' colors are combined,
with gates opening on all four sides corresponding to the east, west, south, and north;
the single central layer does not require a gate to be opened.
Take eight large earthen jars and four smaller pots;
fill them with water and insert cypress and tree branches into them,
then place these vessels within the water jars.
Prepare white cakes, non-glutinous rice porridge, milk curds, clarified butter, honey, fragrant fruits,
and other offerings. Then, light sixteen lamps and insert sixteen unused arrows outside each of the four gates.
Tie five-colored threads to the arrows.
Take four pieces of khadira wood and red sandalwood;
two should be five finger-widths long and two should be six finger-widths long.
Drive stakes into the four corners of the altar.
Scatter various kinds of seasonal and non-seasonal flowers upon the altar.
Furthermore, take one thousand eight hundred pieces of *pāṭala* wood that are small and without fruit.
Each is one foot in length.
Whether it be a clay bowl or a copper bowl,
smear this wooden branch with ghee and milk.
Recite the mantra once for each branch and immediately cast it into the fire.
If *khadira* wood is unavailable, red jujube wood may be used as a substitute. One must also paint an image of the Holy Avalokiteśvara in white.
Perform it according to the size of one's capacity.
Furthermore, the *Fanyifa* (Method for Translating) previously stated:
"Karmic obstructions accumulated over a thousand kalpas."
If one recites and contemplates this at a single time, all [obstacles] will be entirely extinguished.
One shall attain the roots of goodness from the assembly of the thousand Buddhas and reach the limit of turning one's back upon the cycle of birth, old age, sickness, and death for a thousand kalpas.
After casting off this body, one will immediately see a thousand universal wheel-turning kings who constantly uphold the ten wholesome paths of action.
If one wishes to be born in the pure lands of the Buddhas, [one should practice accordingly].
Recite [the mantra] twenty-one times during each of the three periods of both day and night.
When thirty-seven days have been completed, whatever one desires will be fulfilled;
one will either see the golden form of the Buddha or the forms of Bodhisattvas within a dream. This is the preliminary sign by which one knows that they shall be born in the Pure Land.
The aforementioned mantra and its efficacies were both translated from the Sanskrit original by Master *Tongshi* at Zongchi Monastery;
the methods for the mudrās were translated by Master *Kudra*.
The alternative translation states:
Regarding the practice of receiving and upholding the Dharma,
take five *jin* of *tupā* incense along with its sprouts.
One thousand pieces of paper mulberry wood, each one foot long,
together with one thousand recitations of the *su-zong* mantra;
these are to be used when one is about to perform the cremation.
Anoint the wooden stem and the incense with clarified butter (*sarpis*),
reciting the mantra once over each before burning them.
Pre-emptively collect cow dung during the fifth or sixth lunar month and dry it in the shade.
Mix tūba incense with water to form the ground for the ritual site.
Construct a circular site measuring two cubits in diameter.
Upon the site, place various kinds of flowers and incense.
In the winter months, when there are no flowers, one should carve flowers [into the vessel] and place them therein.
Then, the incantation master faces east while burning frankincense.
Recite this while seated until it is completed one thousand times;
the rite is accomplished. Before performing the recitation, consume this consecrated water twenty-one times, or seven times.

The incantation for purifying defilements through water, the incantation for cleansing the chamber, the path, and the Buddha hall, the incantation for washing the body, the incantation for striking illness with willow branches, and the incantation for curing disease through water—all shall be effective.
Each should be recited twenty-one times.
If one can recite this twenty-one times each during the three periods of every day for the duration of one’s life,
the destruction of sins will be inconceivable and it will be effective for all purposes.
This is the Thousand-Turn Dharani, the Mantra of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva.
